items.signal_prefix: President Lee: new-fab capex could go up to $16 billion (US

set.signal: President Lee (who first said '$1.6 billion' and '16 billion NT dollars' before correcting himself to US dollars): new-fab capex 'could go up to' $16 billion US dollars just for one fab - '$16 billion is for 50K' - including construction, clean room, equipment and some EUV for the future.

items.reason: Hedge kept: the president garbled the currency and amount before settling on US$16 billion, and the 50K was his answer to an analyst's 35K prompt; the dividend-policy clause is dividend capital allocation (excluded, skill section 2).
items.evidence: That CapEx could go up to $1.6 billion, I am sorry, $16 billion, right? 16 billion NT dollars. ... $16 billion US dollars, I am sorry ... $16 billion is for 50K.

items.label: Volex Q4 FY2026 (06-26-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO Boaden: EV and Electrification growth was supported by a

set.signal: CFO Boaden: EV and Electrification growth was supported by a full-year contribution from a major vertically integrated charging program for a European charging infrastructure business; Volex is diversifying into energy storage (connecting batteries to solar generation, using EV-like DC voltages and connectors), where CEO Rothschild says cables, connectors and plastics are all made in-house; first-quarter EV demand has been strong as consumers adopt EVs in response to higher fuel costs. CEO Rothschild: when tariff landscapes shifted this year, Volex relocated EV cable production, with no disruption to quality or lead times for customers.

items.reason: Attribution: the EV-cable relocation was said by the CEO in his strategy section, not by the CFO named at the start of the entry.
items.evidence: Nat Rothschild: ... When tariff landscapes shifted this year, we relocated EV cable production, and our customers received that flexibility with no disruption to quality or lead times.

items.label: Xiaomi Q2 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Smart EVs: Xiaomi delivered 104,199 vehicles in Q2 2026, the

set.signal: Smart EVs: Xiaomi delivered 104,199 vehicles in Q2 2026, the sixth consecutive quarter of YoY delivery growth, with Smart EV sales revenue of CNY 23.9 billion; SU7 series ranked first in first-half sales among pure electric sedans priced above CNY 200,000 in mainland China, and cumulative SU7-series deliveries exceeded 500,000 units as of August 17, 2026. CFO Lam: segment gross margin moved on mix - last year's Q2 had higher-margin SU7 Ultra deliveries, the new-generation SU7 (launched in March) has higher costs and a larger delivery share lowered gross margin QoQ, and starting large-model revenue had a negative impact. In a later answer whose speaker is not clearly labelled in the transcript, management said EV ASP is a result of product mix, not a goal, and 'relatively speaking, is not related to GP margin'. Self-developed Xiaomi Titan Alloy 2.0 is mass-produced and applied to the new-generation SU7 and YU7 series.

items.reason: Attribution: the EV ASP answer (JP Morgan question) sits in a turn labelled 'Conference Moderator' with no executive named; the speaker labels in this file are scrambled, so it cannot be pinned on CFO Lam.
items.evidence: That's why I think ASP is a result to us. It's not a goal. ASP, relatively speaking, is not related to GP margin.

items.label: Xiaomi Q2 FY2026 (08-18-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Smartphones (CFO Lam, President William Lu): revenue CNY 42.

set.signal: Smartphones (CFO Lam, President William Lu): revenue CNY 42.1 billion (38.7% of total) on 31.2 million global shipments, down YoY, at a record-high ASP after product-mix optimization and price increases - Lu: ASP rose by almost CNY 300; smartphone gross margin 8.5% in Q2 (9.3% in the first half) despite historically high memory costs. Top three globally for the 24th consecutive quarter (Omdia data), top three in 53 countries and regions and top five in 67; second in Southeast Asia, Latin America and Middle East (19.3%, 16.2% and 13.5% share) and third in Europe and Africa (16.5% and 10.9%); premium smartphones 32.1% of mainland China smartphone sales, a record (third-party data). The Redmi flagship launch was advanced from October to August; Lu, with the launch's sales not yet complete: 'I think more than 62% was 16 plus', ASP CNY 5,000 odd, and versus the last generation 'I think the growth is 60%'.

items.reason: Hedges kept: the president gave the Redmi flagship figures as 'I think' and noted sales were not yet complete.
items.evidence: I think more than 62% was 16 plus, and then the ASP is CNY 5,000 odd. Today, our sales have not been completed yet. Comparing with the last generation, I think the growth is 60%.
